title: Team file library
summary: Build folder and file CRUD with authorized uploads, resumable transfers, versions, and safe cleanup.
outcome: A private file library whose metadata, object storage, permissions, and background processing have explicit consistency rules.
prerequisites: Shared-project permissions, repository Layers, and worker lifecycle. Use a fake object store before adding a real provider.
model: Folder: id, workspaceId, parentId, name, archivedAt. File: id, folderId, currentVersionId, revision.
FileVersion: objectKey, expectedBytes, checksum, status, uploaderId. UploadSession: expiry, parts, state, operationId.
Separate a file's stable identity from immutable versions and temporary upload sessions. Storage keys are generated by the server.
boundaries: Verified membership → file service → database metadata and object-store adapter. An explicit lifecycle reconciles operations spanning the two systems.

milestones.title: Model a navigable folder tree
milestones.brief: Create, rename, move, and archive folders with breadcrumb navigation and protection against cycles or cross-workspace moves.
milestones.explanation: A folder tree requires more than a parentId column. Define root behavior, sibling-name rules, and what archival does to descendants. Moving a folder must reject placing it beneath itself or a descendant. Authorization must cover both source and destination; permission to read a destination does not necessarily imply permission to move content into it.
steps: Write tree fixtures with a root, nested folders, duplicate names, and two workspaces. Define move and archive semantics.
Implement transactional move validation and owner-scoped CRUD. Render breadcrumbs with explicit missing/archived states.
Test cycles, concurrent moves, unknown parents, and permission changes between selection and confirmation.

checks.label: Invalid cycles and cross-workspace moves cannot commit.
Breadcrumbs and child lists agree after a move.
Archival follows the declared descendant policy without losing history.

milestones.experiment: Move A under B while another client moves B under A. Verify the storage boundary preserves the tree invariant.
milestones.review: Explain the invariant independently of the chosen tree representation. Ask the agent to demonstrate a direct service call that bypasses the UI picker safely.
milestones.stretch: Add a bulk move preview with counts and an explicit policy for name collisions.

milestones.title: Authorize an upload intent
milestones.brief: Create a short-lived upload capability only after validating folder access, declared size, type, and a server-generated destination key.
milestones.explanation: A client filename is display text, not a trusted storage path. Generate object keys within a controlled namespace and keep the intended metadata separate from an unverified object. Capabilities should be narrowly scoped and expire; finalization must verify the actual uploaded object rather than trusting the earlier declaration.
steps: Model pending upload metadata and limits. Define allowed types, maximum size, expiry, and overwrite behavior.
Issue upload intents from verified identity through an object-store service Layer. Keep provider credentials on the server.
Test oversized declarations, hostile filenames, unauthorized folders, and expired intents with a controllable clock.

checks.label: Only authorized callers receive scoped upload capabilities.
Client filenames cannot choose arbitrary storage keys.
Pending uploads are distinguishable from ready files.

milestones.experiment: Declare a small allowed file but upload a larger object through the fake provider. Verify finalization catches the mismatch.
milestones.review: Review the provider's actual size/type enforcement separately from your metadata checks. A browser accept attribute is not a security boundary.
milestones.stretch: Bind an upload intent to an expected checksum and verify provider support before relying on it.

milestones.title: Resume interrupted uploads
milestones.brief: Resume a multi-part upload after a connection failure without duplicating parts or publishing an incomplete file.
milestones.explanation: A resumable upload has durable session identity and an authoritative part inventory. The client can propose progress, but the server or storage provider determines which parts exist. Bound concurrent transfers and preserve enough metadata to retry safely. Progress should describe confirmed bytes, not merely bytes queued by the interface.
steps: Define session creation, part receipt, resume, abort, and finalize states using a local fake store. Specify part-number and size constraints.
Implement bounded part transfer and resume from confirmed receipts. Persist the session reference without storing privileged capabilities indefinitely.
Interrupt after several parts, restart the client, and retry one part. Test abort and expiry while a part is in flight.

checks.label: Resume transfers only missing or explicitly replaced parts.
An incomplete upload cannot become a ready version.
Active transfers stay within the configured concurrency bound.

milestones.experiment: Lose the response for an accepted part and retry it. Verify the same part identity does not inflate confirmed byte counts.
milestones.review: Explain which side is authoritative for each progress number. Distinguish client cancellation from provider-side cleanup of retained parts.
milestones.stretch: Add per-file fairness so one large upload does not monopolize all available transfer slots.

milestones.title: Publish a verified file version
milestones.brief: Verify a completed object and publish an immutable version only after required checks have passed.
milestones.explanation: Database and object-store writes do not share a normal SQL transaction. Represent intermediate states explicitly and make finalization retryable. If inspection is asynchronous, keep the object unavailable until the result is accepted. A callback must identify the exact object version so an old result cannot approve newer content.
steps: Define pending, uploaded, inspecting, ready, and rejected states. Write allowed transitions and cleanup behavior for each.
Verify object metadata and enqueue inspection after upload. Publish a currentVersionId only through an authorized, conditional transition.
Test duplicate finalization, stale inspection callbacks, failed database writes, and a rejected file followed by a clean new version.

checks.label: Only the exact verified object version becomes downloadable.
Duplicate callbacks cannot publish or charge work twice.
Rejected and abandoned objects have a recoverable cleanup path.

milestones.experiment: Deliver a clean inspection result for version one after version two has replaced the pending upload. Verify the callback cannot approve version two accidentally.
milestones.review: List the intermediate states visible after every injected failure. Do not present object deletion as an automatic consequence of database rollback.
milestones.stretch: Add a reconciliation job that finds uploaded objects with no valid metadata reference.

milestones.title: Download private content safely
milestones.brief: Issue downloads for the current authorized file version and preserve access rules across preview, history, and direct-link endpoints.
milestones.explanation: Checking access only on the file list leaves direct download endpoints exposed. Validate current membership before issuing a short-lived capability and decide how revocation interacts with already issued URLs. File previews and historical versions need the same deliberate policy; obscurity of a storage key is not authorization.
steps: Write an access matrix for folder members, outsiders, uploaders, and administrators across current and historical versions.
Implement authorized download and preview issuance with bounded expiry. Render filenames safely and define the disposition for untrusted content.
Test guessed IDs, revoked access, archived folders, and old signed links under the documented revocation limitation.

checks.label: Direct download and preview endpoints enforce the access matrix.
Capabilities expire and do not disclose storage credentials.
Historical versions follow an explicit permission policy.

milestones.experiment: Revoke a user's membership after issuing a download URL. Measure its remaining validity and compare it with the promised security behavior.
milestones.review: If immediate revocation is required, explain why short expiry alone may be insufficient and evaluate a mediated download route.
milestones.stretch: Add rate and byte limits to bulk downloads and test that one workspace cannot exhaust shared resources.

milestones.title: Version, restore, and clean up files
milestones.brief: Support restoring an older version and removing unreferenced objects without deleting a version still used by another operation.
milestones.explanation: Logical deletion and physical object removal occur at different times. Define retention windows and references before building cleanup. A job must recheck eligibility before deleting because a version can become current again after the job was queued. Keep cleanup receipts and make retries safe when an object is already absent.
steps: Specify archive, restore-version, and permanent-cleanup policies. Create fixtures with shared references, pending uploads, and current historical versions.
Implement a version-aware restore command and bounded cleanup jobs. Recheck reference and retention conditions immediately before destructive provider actions.
Race restore against cleanup in a disposable store, restart cleanup after failure, and restore database metadata alongside object fixtures.

checks.label: Restoring a version preserves file identity and an accurate history.
Cleanup never deletes an object still referenced under the declared policy.
Retries tolerate already removed objects and retain diagnostic receipts.

milestones.experiment: Queue an old version for cleanup, restore it as current, then execute the delayed job. Verify the current reference protects it.
milestones.review: Document what a database backup does not include. Recovery must account for object versions, retention, and provider lifecycle rules too.
milestones.stretch: Produce a dry-run cleanup report and compare its proposed removals with the eventual committed receipts.
